path.description: Path to file or directory (absolute or relative to project root)

startLine.description: 1-based line or directory entry to start reading from

endLine.description: 1-based line or directory entry to stop reading at (inclusive)

limit.description: Max lines (default: 2000) or directory entries (default and cap: 1000) to return

offset.description: 1-based line or directory entry to start reading from (use with limit). Ignored if startLine is provided

ref.description: Git revision to read the file at instead of the working tree: a branch, tag, full or short commit SHA, or a form like HEAD~2. Content comes from git's object store; the working tree, index and HEAD are not touched.

read.description:
Read file contents or list directory entries.

Use either startLine/endLine OR offset/limit to read a section of a file or sorted directory listing.

Behavior:
- Returns line-numbered content (e.g., "1: const x = 1")
- Lines longer than 2000 characters are truncated
- Output capped at 50KB
- Binary files are auto-detected and return a size-only message
- Supported images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) and PDFs are returned as tool attachments; range arguments are ignored for media
- Directories return sorted entries with trailing / for subdirectories; offset is 1-based, limit defaults to and is capped at 1000 entries. Enumeration stops at 10,000 entries; partial listings carry a shown/total trailer.

Pass `ref` to read the file as it is at a git revision (branch, tag, SHA, HEAD~2); the reply's first line names the commit it resolved to.

Examples:
  Read full file: { "path": "src/app.ts" }
  Read lines 50-100: { "path": "src/app.ts", "startLine": 50, "endLine": 100 }
  Read 30 lines from line 200: { "path": "src/app.ts", "offset": 200, "limit": 30 }
  List directory: { "path": "src/" }

target.description: What to outline: a file path, directory path, URL, or array of paths. The mode is auto-detected: URLs by `http://`/`https://` prefix, directories by stat, arrays as multi-file.

files.description: Directory-only mode: when true, target must be a directory or array of directories and the result is a breadth-first file tree with directory rollups plus language, symbol, and line counts.

includeTests.description: Directory outline only: include test files. Defaults to false; tests are hidden.

ref.description: Git revision to read the file at instead of the working tree: a branch, tag, full or short commit SHA, or a form like HEAD~2. Content comes from git's object store; the working tree, index and HEAD are not touched.

outline.description:
Structural outline of source code, documentation files, or remote URLs. For code, returns symbols (functions, classes, types) with line ranges. For Markdown and HTML, returns heading hierarchy. Use this to explore structure before reading specific sections with aft_zoom. With `files: true`, the outline is breadth-first with directory rollups; drill in by outlining a subdirectory. Rows show language, symbol count, and line count.

For understanding a specific feature, prefer aft_search + aft_zoom on named symbols; use aft_outline on a whole directory only for high-level structure mapping. aft_zoom with `callgraph:true` gives one-level forward calls-out; use aft_callgraph only for reverse callers or multi-level traces.

Pass a single `target`:
  • file path → outline that file (with signatures)
  • directory path → outline source files under it
  • URL (http:// or https://) → fetch and outline a remote HTML/Markdown document
  • array of paths → outline multiple files in one call; with files:true, every path must be a directory

When a list is cut, the reply ends with `shown N of M <unit> (<reason>) · narrow: <knobs>`; absence of that line means the list is complete.

Pass `ref` to read the file as it is at a git revision (branch, tag, SHA, HEAD~2); the reply's first line names the commit it resolved to. Only a single file can be outlined at a revision.

batch.description: One or more lookups; entries may mix file paths and URLs

target.description: File path (absolute or project-relative) or HTTP/HTTPS URL, auto-detected; issue://N or pr://N when GitHub reads are enabled

symbols.description: Symbol name for code or heading text for Markdown/HTML; a string or array of strings

contextLines.description: Lines of context before/after each symbol (default: 3)

callgraph.description: Include call-graph annotations for every entry (default: false)

ref.description: Git revision to read the file at instead of the working tree: a branch, tag, full or short commit SHA, or a form like HEAD~2. Content comes from git's object store; the working tree, index and HEAD are not touched.

zoom.description:
Inspect code symbols or documentation sections. Pass lookups in `batch: [{ target, symbols }]`; a single lookup is a one-entry batch. Mix files and URLs in one batch, for example `batch: [{ target: "src/app.ts", symbols: "run" }, { target: "https://example.com/docs", symbols: "Overview" }]`. Each target is auto-detected as a file path or an HTTP/HTTPS URL. `symbols` is a string or string array. Markdown and HTML lookups return the section under the heading. Top-level `contextLines` and `callgraph` apply to every entry; callgraph adds calls-out and called-by annotations. Each failed lookup reports its own error line.

Pass `ref` to read the file as it is at a git revision (branch, tag, SHA, HEAD~2); the reply's first line names the commit it resolved to. Every file of the call is read at that revision; URLs do not have revisions.
